standard_prerequisites.name: The auxiliary finite morphism over an irreducible closed subspace, and the projection formula for an affine morphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, labels lemma-finite-morphism-Noetherian (invoked at proof lines 4169 and 4173) and lemma-affine-morphism-projection-ideal (invoked at proof line 4179)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first provides $Z'$ with the finite morphisms $i' : Z' \to Y$ and $f' : Z' \to Z$ and the support property (3)(a); the second gives $f'_*\mathcal{I}' = \mathcal{I}\mathcal{G}$, which identifies the subsheaf $\mathcal{G}'$ used in (3)(b).

standard_prerequisites.name: Coherence of the relevant pushforwards and vanishing of the higher direct images of the finite morphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, labels lemma-finite-pushforward-coherent (invoked at proof line 4188), lemma-i-star-equivalence (invoked at proof line 4189) and lemma-finite-higher-direct-image-zero (invoked at proof line 4220), together with the projection formula and the Leray spectral sequence of Cohomology on Sites (proof lines 4216-4219)
standard_prerequisites.use: They let the cohomology of $i_*\mathcal{G}' \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}$ on $X$ be rewritten as the cohomology of $i'_*\mathcal{I}' \otimes f^*\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n}$ on the scheme $Y$, where the vanishing for $n \geq n_0$ is known.

core_obligations: Prove (1) $\Rightarrow$ (2): a finite morphism is representable by schemes, so $Y$ is a scheme, and the scheme case of the equivalence gives ampleness of $f^*\mathcal{L}$ (proof lines 4146-4150).

For (2) $\Rightarrow$ (1), introduce the property $P$ on coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules: vanishing of $H^p(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$ for all $n \geq n_0$ and $p > 0$; conclude ampleness of $\mathcal{L}$ from $P$ by the cohomological criterion (proof lines 4152-4158).

Verify conditions (1) and (2) of the reduction criterion for $P$: two-out-of-three from the long exact cohomology sequence and exactness of tensoring with an invertible sheaf, and stability under direct sums from additivity of $H^p(X,-)$ (proof lines 4159-4164).

Verify condition (3): for a reduced irreducible closed $i : Z \to X$ take $Z'$, $i'$, $f'$ as supplied and $\mathcal{G} = f'_*\mathcal{O}_{Z'}$, whose support is $Z$; for a nonzero ideal $\mathcal{I}$ put $\mathcal{G}' = \mathcal{I}\mathcal{G} = f'_*\mathcal{I}'$, note that $\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{G}'$ is supported in the proper closed subset cut out by $\mathcal{I}$, and check that $P$ holds for $i_*\mathcal{G}'$ (proof lines 4166-4186).

Establish the last point by the chain of equalities rewriting $H^p(X, i_*\mathcal{G}' \otimes \mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$ as $H^p(Y, i'_*\mathcal{I}' \otimes f^*\mathcal{L}^{\otimes n})$, using the projection formula, the Leray spectral sequence and the vanishing of the higher direct images of the finite morphism, and then cutting off at the integer $n_0$ that ampleness of $f^*\mathcal{L}$ provides on the scheme $Y$ (proof lines 4187-4222).
proof_roadmap: The implication (1) $\Rightarrow$ (2) via representability of finite morphisms (proof lines 4146-4150).
The property $P$ and its relation to ampleness (proof lines 4152-4158).
Condition (3): the sheaf $\mathcal{G}$ on an irreducible support and the choice of $\mathcal{G}'$ (proof lines 4166-4186).
The cohomology computation on $Y$ and the cutoff $n_0$ (proof lines 4187-4222).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a finite surjective morphism of algebraic spaces proper over a Noetherian ring, ampleness of an invertible sheaf is equivalent to ampleness of its pullback, together with the scheme-theoretic nature of the source (statement lines 4133-4143). One implication is immediate from representability of finite morphisms and the scheme case; for the other the proof sets up the cohomological vanishing property, feeds it through the criterion for properties of coherent sheaves on a Noetherian space, and in the remaining condition analyses the behaviour of an ideal on an irreducible support through an auxiliary finite cover and a chain of equalities using the projection formula and Leray. The verification of condition (3) is the substance, so the claim is H2.
